record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: level-set geometry for cmc Dirichlet solutions
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded convex domain, and let u solve the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du / sqrt(1 + |Du|²)) = 2H in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. How can one control the distribution of the convex level curves of u in terms of H? Can Wang’s counterexample on convexity of level sets be extended to the case where Ω is unbounded?

evidence.quote: A method to find H-surfaces spanning a given curve is by solving the Dirichlet problem { div Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)=2H in Ω; u=φ in ∂Ω }.

Problem 4.2. Suppose that Ω is a bounded convex domain. Let u be a solution (4.1) for φ=0 on ∂Ω. Give a control of the distribution of the convex level curves in terms of the value H. Extend the Wang’s example, if possible, when Ω is not bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain and let $H > 0$ be a constant. Let $u \in C^2(\Omega) \cap C(\overline{\Omega})$ be a solution of the constant mean curvature Dirichlet problem
$$\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{Du}{\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}}\right) = 2H \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega.$$
The graph of $u$ is then a surface of constant mean curvature $H$ spanning $\partial\Omega$. It is known (by an example of X.-J. Wang) that even when $\Omega$ is smooth and uniformly convex, the level sets $\{u = c\}$ need not all be convex.

(a) Establish quantitative control, in terms of the value $H$ (and the geometry of $\Omega$), of the distribution inside $\Omega$ of those level curves $\{u = c\}$ which are convex: identify the range of heights $c \in (0, \max_\Omega u)$ for which $\{u = c\}$ is a convex curve, and describe how this range depends on $H$.

(b) Determine whether the counterexample of Wang to the convexity of level sets can be extended to the setting in which $\Omega$ is an unbounded convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, i.e., whether there exists an unbounded convex domain $\Omega$ and a solution $u$ of the above Dirichlet problem (with $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$) whose level sets are not all convex.
artifact.category_tag: Constant mean curvature equation / level set convexity
artifact.status_search_result: Wang's counterexample to the convexity of level sets of solutions to the constant mean curvature equation in a smooth uniformly convex bounded domain is established (JEMS 2014). However, no quantitative description of the distribution of convex level curves in terms of H, nor an extension of the counterexample to unbounded convex domains, was found in the literature; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to the convexity of level sets of solutions to the mean curvature equation
status_evidence.snippet: Wang shows there exists a bounded smooth uniformly convex domain whose CMC Dirichlet solution has nonconvex level sets.
status_evidence.claim: Wang's counterexample exists for bounded convex domains.

status_evidence.title: Convexity of level sets for elliptic problems in convex domains or convex rings: two counterexamples
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to convexity of level sets for elliptic problems in convex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Related counterexamples in bounded convex domain setting; no extension to unbounded domains is provided.
